## Test suite and continuous integration (`ctest`, `pytest`, the `build-and-test` CI job) {#sec-ch10-test-suite}

### Summary

pyharp's tests are of two kinds: C++ programs built with GoogleTest and run by `ctest`, and Python files run by
`pytest`. A reader who wants to know what is verified needs three lists: the tests that exist in the tree, the tests
the build registers, and the tests the continuous-integration job runs. This section gives the three lists at the
pin, the result of running every test that exists, and what that shows about coverage.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** What pyharp's test files check, and which of them CI runs (Tests layer).

**Data.** 22 C++ test files, 7 Python files in `tests/`, 15 in `tests/spectra/`.

**Placement.** `ctest` after a CMake build with `BUILD_TESTS=ON`; `pytest` from the source root.

**Activation.** CMake option `BUILD_TESTS` (default on); CI on every push to `main` and every change proposed against it.

**Guarantee / limits.** CI runs 14 C++ test programs and 3 Python files; the other 27 files are not run.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer of @sec-ch10-test-suite.
:::

Local symbols: none.

The C++ tests are registered one by one with the CMake macro `setup_test`; a file that is not named there is
neither built nor run. The Python test files are copied into the build tree but never registered with `ctest`.
The CI job builds the tests, runs `ctest`, and runs three files of `tests/spectra/` with `pytest`.

### Derivation

None: this section states facts about the test harness and has no equations.

### Numerical method

The method here is the harness itself. `setup_test` builds `tests/<name>.cpp` into an executable
`<name>.<build type>` linked against the pyharp library and `gtest_main`, and registers it with `add_test`
(`setup_test`, {{< code cmake/macros/macro_setup_test.cmake repo=pyharp >}}). `tests/CMakeLists.txt`
({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt repo=pyharp >}}) calls it for 14 files; it copies every `tests/*.py` into the build
tree with `configure_file`, but its `add_test(... pytest ...)` line is commented out. The workflow
({{< code .github/workflows/ci.yml repo=pyharp >}}) has one test job, `build-and-test`, on `ubuntu-latest` and
`macOS-latest` with Python 3.11, torch 2.10.0 (the CPU wheel on Linux) and `pydisort==1.7.1` installed with
`--no-deps`; it configures with `-DNETCDF=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON`, runs `ctest --output-on-failure`, and runs
`pytest` on `tests/spectra/test_hitemp_lines.py`, `test_line_kernel.py` and `test_hitran_lines.py`. No job builds
with CUDA.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch10-test-suite-coverage
#| fig-cap: "Test files at the pin by category: how many exist (light bars), how many ctest registers (hatched), and how many the CI job runs (dark bars). C++ files that ctest registers are run by CI through ctest; Python files are run only if the workflow names them."
#| fig-alt: "Grouped bar chart. C++: 22 files exist, 14 registered, 14 run by CI. Python tests directory: 7 exist, 0 registered, 0 run. Python tests/spectra: 15 exist, 0 registered, 3 run by CI."
#| echo: false
from pyharp_report.ch10.figures.fig_test_suite_coverage import make_fig
make_fig()
```

Many of the C++ tests are parametrised over device and precision by the fixture `DeviceTest`
({{< code tests/device_testing.hpp DeviceTest repo=pyharp >}}): CPU float32, CPU float64, CUDA float32 and CUDA
float64. `DeviceTest::SetUp` ({{< code tests/device_testing.hpp DeviceTest::SetUp repo=pyharp >}}) skips the CUDA
cases when `torch::cuda::is_available()` is false. The skip tests the torch installation, not whether pyharp was
built with CUDA, so a CPU-only pyharp linked against a CUDA-enabled torch on a machine with a GPU runs the CUDA
cases and fails them (Tests layer below).

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| test registration | {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt repo=pyharp >}} | `setup_test(...)` lines | `BUILD_TESTS` |
| build and register one test | {{< code cmake/macros/macro_setup_test.cmake repo=pyharp >}} | `setup_test` | always |
| device/precision fixture | {{< code tests/device_testing.hpp DeviceTest repo=pyharp >}} | `DeviceTest` | always |
| CUDA skip rule | {{< code tests/device_testing.hpp DeviceTest::SetUp repo=pyharp >}} | `DeviceTest::SetUp` | torch CUDA |
| CI job | {{< code .github/workflows/ci.yml repo=pyharp >}} | `build-and-test` | changes to `main` |

: Code map of the test harness. {#tbl-ch10-test-suite-code}

1. CMake configures with `BUILD_TESTS=ON` (the default) and adds `tests/` ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt repo=pyharp >}}).
2. Each `setup_test(<name>)` builds and registers `<name>.release` in a Release build
   ({{< code cmake/macros/macro_setup_test.cmake repo=pyharp >}}); `setup_test(test_yaml_input)` is
   commented out.
3. The workflow ({{< code .github/workflows/ci.yml repo=pyharp >}}) installs the package and runs `ctest` and the
   three `pytest` files; a failure in any step fails the job.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_inventory.py` `[I1]`-`[I3]` | which files exist, are registered, are run by CI | exact | file listing |
| `run_suite.sh` `[S1]`, `[S2]` | `ctest` with GPUs visible and hidden | pass count | `ctest` |
| `run_suite.sh` `[S3]` | the 8 unregistered C++ files, built out of tree | builds, exit | compiler, gtest |
| `run_suite.sh` `[S4]`, `[S5]` | every Python test file | pass count | `pytest` |

: Checks of the test suite. {#tbl-ch10-test-suite-tests}

The inventory: 22 C++ test files, of which `ctest` registers 14; 3 of the 22 contain no assertion macro
(`test_composition.cpp`, `test_hypsometric.cpp`, `test_yaml_input.cpp`), and `test_bbflux.cpp` asserts only
output shapes. None of the 7 files in `tests/` and 3 of the 15 in `tests/spectra/` are run by CI[^ch10-inv].

Running everything on two source builds of the pin (one against pydisort 1.7.1, one against 1.8.13), on CPU:

- `ctest` passes 14 of 14 with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=` set, as on CI's CPU-only runners; with the GPUs visible it
  passes 11 of 14, because the CUDA cases of `test_toon.release`, `test_water_liquid_mie.release` and
  `test_water_cloud_temperature.release` raise "missing kernel for cuda" on a pyharp built without CUDA[^ch10-run].
- Of the 8 unregistered C++ files, 5 do not compile (`application/application.hpp` is not in the tree), 1 does not
  compile against the current API (`test_yaml_input.cpp`), 1 builds and fails all 3 of its tests (its input
  `example_infrared.yaml` is not in the tree), and 1 builds and exits 0 with no assertion
  (`test_composition.cpp`)[^ch10-run].
- The 7 top-level Python files: 13 tests pass and 1 fails, `test_sonora2020.py`, whose data file must be fetched
  first[^ch10-run].
- The 15 spectra files from the source root: 11 files pass; 8 tests fail in 4 files that CI does not run
  (`test_atm_overview_cli.py` 3, `test_cli.py` 2, `test_output_names.py` 2, `test_molecule_plot_cli.py` 1). Of CI's
  three files, `test_hitemp_lines.py::test_prepare_reads_zip_and_bz2_and_reuses_cache` failed 2 times in 50 runs
  (once in the committed outputs, in the pairing built against 1.8.13 and run with 1.7.1), asserting that a
  rewritten file has a new modification time[^ch10-run].

Apart from that intermittent failure and the abort of @sec-ch10-packaging, the results are the same for both builds
and for the two mixed pairings.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A green CI run covers the 14 registered C++ programs and 3 spectra files only; the Python tests of the solvers,
including `tests/test_toon.py`, are not run.
:::

- **CI coverage (CANDIDATE, test registration).** 27 of the 44 test files are not run by CI: 8 C++ files are not
  registered and 19 Python files are not named in the workflow[^ch10-inv]. 7 of the 8 unregistered C++ files do
  not build or do not pass, and 8 tests in 4 unrun spectra files fail[^ch10-run].
- **Device gate (CANDIDATE, test fixture).** The CUDA cases run whenever torch reports a GPU, whether or not pyharp
  has CUDA kernels; 3 of 14 `ctest` programs then fail on a CPU-only build[^ch10-run].
- **Assertion-free tests.** `test_hypsometric.release` is registered and asserts nothing; `test_bbflux.release`
  asserts shapes only; the gtest `DeviceTest.simple_toon_mckay89` of `tests/test_toon.cpp` has no assertion.
- **Flaky test.** `test_hitemp_lines.py::test_prepare_reads_zip_and_bz2_and_reuses_cache` depends on the file
  system giving two writes different modification times; it failed 2 times in 50 runs on a `tmpfs` temporary
  directory. That the cause is timestamp resolution is a hypothesis; it was not isolated.
- **Untested combinations.** No CUDA build was available; GPU coverage: answered at @sec-ch09.
